summary: Describes how the IETF picks its representative for the ICANN Root Zone Evolution Review Committee (RZERC). It is a process memo about an appointment, not a technical protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: The Root Zone Evolution Review Committee reviews proposed changes to the DNS root zone and advises the ICANN Board. This RFC explains how the IETF Architecture Board selects the IETF's member of that committee.

subtitle: How the IAB selects the IETF's member of ICANN's RZERC.

tldr.problem: The RZERC charter calls on the IETF to name a delegate, so the IETF needs a selection process.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB solicits nominations and selects one person for a one-year term, which may be renewed for up to three additional one-year terms.
tldr.outcome: The memo sets out candidate qualifications, the annual timetable and an optional process for filling a vacancy early.

facts.label: Possible renewals
facts.value: Up to three additional one-year terms

sections.title: The Committee and the IETF's Role
sections.content:
The ICANN Root Zone Evolution Review Committee (RZERC) reviews proposed architectural changes to the DNS root zone, the systems used to make those changes, and the ways the root zone is distributed. It makes recommendations to the ICANN Board.

The RZERC charter calls on the IETF to name a delegate. RFC 8128 describes how the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) gathers input and selects that person.
sections.plainLanguage: The RZERC reviews proposed changes to the DNS root zone and advises the ICANN Board. The IETF names one member, and this RFC explains how the IAB chooses that person.

sections.title: Qualifications for the Member
sections.content:
A candidate should have clear involvement in the IETF, especially active participation in its working groups. The candidate is expected to understand Internet technology related to the DNS root zone and explain technical issues to the ICANN Board.

The candidate should also understand the roles and responsibilities of both the IETF and ICANN. As the IETF's delegate, the person is expected to call on experts in the IETF community when needed.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF's member should know its work and understand technology related to the DNS root zone. The person should explain technical issues clearly and know when to ask IETF experts for help.

sections.title: Term, Nominations and Selection
sections.content:
The appointment lasts one year and may be renewed for up to three additional one-year terms. If an eligible incumbent wants to continue, the IAB may seek community feedback and reappoint that person if it decides a full selection process is unnecessary.

Otherwise, the IAB calls for nominations publicly on the IETF Announce mailing list. Self-nominations are allowed, and all IETF participants may be nominated. The IAB publishes the nominees, reviews their material and selects a member; IAB members who accept nominations leave the selection discussions.
sections.plainLanguage: The member serves one year and may be appointed again within the stated term limit. The IAB invites nominations, including self-nominations, and reviews candidates before choosing one.

sections.title: Schedule and Mid-term Vacancies
sections.content:
The IAB aims to seat new members in time for ICANN's annual general meeting in Q4. It allows 4-6 weeks for nominations or an incumbent review and another 4-6 weeks for reviewing nominees and selecting a member. The IAB announces the specific dates in Q2.

If a member cannot finish a term, the IAB may select a replacement for the remaining term using a separately announced interim timeline. Otherwise, the next annual selection fills the vacancy.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAB plans the yearly selection so a new member can take a seat by ICANN's annual meeting. If someone leaves early, the IAB can choose a replacement or fill the place in the next yearly selection.
